title: Freeze recovery inventory class contract and quarantine record
description: Objective: resolve the current contradictory inventory cardinality and define the durable fail-closed reconciliation/quarantine record the coordinator can persist. Deliverable: one canonical daemon recovery-inventory contract that maps every detailed external population to exactly one configured proof class, defines ABSENT/ADOPTED/QUARANTINED/UNKNOWN dispositions and upstream-code retention, and provides a frozen digest-verified persisted record bound to project, backup cursor/generation, selected incarnation/key epoch and quarantine refs. MEASURED GAP at HEAD c0c5929: design line 978 names seven populations, CORE-S14 names six grouped categories, @moe/runner exposes four combined node classes, adding scheduler resource yields five proof classes, the coordinator description lists six groups, and DoD demands seven generated classes; the runner collector rejects unknown/extra classes. No production quarantine/reconciliation record or sink exists. Consumer: task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa and downstream task-6f786c58cabf4f85be8ed4135e68a752. NOT in scope: enumerating providers, invoking adapters, allocating authority, or approving recovery.complete. Owned paths: focused daemon recovery contract/codec/persistence modules and tests, plus minimal store schema only if required. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: A frozen hand-written class/population mapping resolves the 4-runner/5-proof/6-scenario/7-population ambiguity: every design population is covered exactly once, no proof is duplicated to inflate cardinality, and unknown/duplicate/omitted/extra classes refuse with stable code/layer.

The contract defines canonical ABSENT, ADOPTED, QUARANTINED and UNKNOWN dispositions; ADOPTED requires exact restored intent plus current incarnation/key epoch, unmatched items can only quarantine/UNKNOWN, and no disposition invents history or retry authority.

A durable frozen reconciliation record binds project, backup cursor and generation, selected incarnation and key epoch, configured class mapping, source proof digests, every item disposition, retained upstream code/layer and quarantine refs; any byte change changes or invalidates its digest.

Missing inventory, incomplete coverage, non-fenceable state, artifact/key proof failure and unresolved items persist truth UNKNOWN with coordinator code UNKNOWN_TRUTH at RECOVERY_INVENTORY while retaining the precise upstream code/layer separately.
Persistence/reopen and hostile-byte tests drive the real store/codec surface, assert exact cardinalities and stable code/layer, and generated cases assert a non-zero exact population count.

Mutation drills alter canonical digest input and one adoption/incarnation comparison and turn named tests red; fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not satisfy the seven-population requirement by duplicating a combined runner proof; the mapping must be explicit and one-to-one at the semantic population level.
Do not narrow the design or accept caller-selected current binding; use exact selected store/anchor authority in consumers.
Retain upstream code and layer separately from the coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY answer; never restamp away provenance.
Shared schema changes require full regression and crash/reopen evidence.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the focused contract and exact LF NodeNext bridge. Freeze ordered proof classes as `PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK`, `RESOURCE`, `WORKSPACE`, `INTEGRATION_TARGET`, `GIT_INTEGRATION_ON_DISK`, `ARTIFACT_OBJECT_STAGING`; freeze the seven design populations and the explicit class-to-population rows, with only the provider class containing two populations. Define closed proof/truth/disposition/result vocabularies, precise mapping error codes (`RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CLASS_EXTRA|UNKNOWN|DUPLICATE|OMITTED`), coordinator `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`, layer `RECOVERY_INVENTORY`, ledger upstream codes/layer, bounds, and immutable record/input/result types. Closed vocabularies: RECOVERY_INVENTORY_TRUTHS (COMPLETE, UNKNOWN — UNKNOWN is the floor); RECOVERY_INVENTORY_DISPOSITIONS (ABSENT, CANCELLED, ADOPTED, QUARANTINED, UNKNOWN) with CANCELLED documented as terminal proof-bearing and explicitly retry/history-free; RECOVERY_INVENTORY_UPSTREAM_LAYERS (RECOVERY_INVENTORY, RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER, INVENTORY_ADAPTER); RECOVERY_INVENTORY_UPSTREAM_CODES (24 codes) containing the four mapping codes RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CLASS_{EXTRA,UNKNOWN,DUPLICATE,OMITTED}, the adjudication/adoption/codec codes, and the ledger codes RECORD_NOT_FOUND / RECORD_UNREADABLE / RECORD_CONFLICT / RECOVERY_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE / RECOVERY_ANCHOR_UNAVAILABLE / RECOVERY_BINDING_MISMATCH.

Immutable types: RecoveryReconciliationProof (class, populations, truth, sourceProofDigest, itemCount, upstream), RecoveryReconciliationItem (class, population, identity, disposition, sourceProofDigest, terminalProofDigest, restoredIntentRef, restoredIntentDigest, quarantineRef, upstream), RecoveryReconciliationRecord binding project/projectTag/backupCursor/backupGenerationDigest/incarnationRef/keyEpochRef/anchorBindingDigest/configuredClasses/proofs/items/truth/coordinator/upstream/recordDigest. implementationPlan.description: Implement total record normalization/adjudication and its exact LF bridge. Validate hostile inputs with own enumerable data descriptors before property access; require the exact configured six-class set and normalize a missing/incomplete configured proof into its canonical UNKNOWN proof slot rather than shrinking the mapping. Bind each subject to its one mapped proof, project/project-tag, verified backup cursor+generation, selected anchor binding digest/incarnation/key epoch, source proof digest, restored-intent reference/digest, terminal proof or quarantine reference, disposition, and separate coordinator/upstream refusal tuples. Enforce: ABSENT only from complete negative proof; CANCELLED only from terminal cancellation proof; ADOPTED only when external/restored identity and both selected recovery refs match exactly; unmatched items only QUARANTINED or UNKNOWN; any incomplete/non-fenceable/artifact-or-key/unresolved fact makes the persisted truth `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`/`RECOVERY_INVENTORY`. Deep-freeze copied data and expose no secret/message bytes.
implementationPlan.note:
Record normalization/adjudication landed, with one disclosed factoring deviation.

DEVIATION (disclosed, not hidden): the step planned one module. It landed as TWO — recovery-inventory-record.ts (240 lines) and recovery-inventory-subject.ts (296 lines) — plus their two exact LF bridges, taking the owned-path count from the plan's ten to twelve. FORCED BY THE BINDING RAIL, and provable: the two responsibilities together measure ~536 physical lines, so a single module would sit at ~536, far past the 400 hard split point epic rail 5 sets. Splitting at the natural seam (record = assembly/ordering/coverage; subject = "is this even a subject, and what does its evidence prove") is the smallest split that clears it. record.ts re-exports every subject type, so consumers still import one module. Both files are under 400; subject.ts is 46 over the 250 target and I did not manufacture a third artificial seam to hide that.

recovery-inventory-subject.ts:
- exactDataRecord (added to the contract this step, 24 lines) reads own enumerable DATA descriptors ONCE, before any property access, and refuses extra/missing/inherited keys and any accessor. An accessor or proxy cannot answer differently on a second read, and a smuggled key is refused rather than dropped — dropping one silently would look like it had been honoured.
- Per-kind exact evidence key sets (EVIDENCE_KEYS), hex64 refs, NFC-normalised bounded control-character-free text, bounded arrays at MAX_RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_ITEMS, and closed-vocabulary upstream {code, layer} reading. readProof accepts only COMPLETE/UNKNOWN.
- adjudicateSubject is the ONE adoption rule: NEGATIVE_COMPLETE -> ABSENT with its terminal proof digest; TERMINAL_CANCELLED -> CANCELLED with its terminal proof digest and no retry field; ORPHAN -> QUARANTINED with its quarantine ref; UNRESOLVED -> UNKNOWN carrying the upstream tuple verbatim. RESTORED_INTENT reaches ADOPTED only when the intent names this exact external identity AND was restored under BOTH currently selected refs; each single deviation quarantines with its own code (ADOPTION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, then ADOPTION_INCARNATION_STALE, then ADOPTION_KEY_EPOCH_STALE). No arm invents history and no arm returns retry authority.

recovery-inventory-record.ts:
- Total by construction: every path returns a record or a frozen refusal, nothing throws.
- refuseConfiguredClasses requires EXACTLY the frozen six, with distinct codes for UNKNOWN, DUPLICATE, EXTRA and OMITTED. A malformed class set is a STRUCTURAL refusal; missing evidence for a well-formed class is NOT — normaliseProofs emits a canonical UNKNOWN slot (digest 0*64, upstream PROOF_MISSING) for every configured class the caller supplied no proof for, so the mapping is always six rows and a caller cannot shrink it by declining to configure a class. No path raises a slot to COMPLETE.
- Each subject is bound to its ONE mapped proof class: a subject whose population is not covered by its declared class refuses POPULATION_UNMAPPED; two subjects on one class-scoped identity refuse SUBJECT_DUPLICATE.
- Item order is deterministic (class index, declared population index, identity), so the same facts in any caller order produce identical bytes.
- truth is UNKNOWN when any proof is UNKNOWN or any item is UNKNOWN; coordinator is then {UNKNOWN_TRUTH, RECOVERY_INVENTORY} and record-level upstream retains PROOF_INCOMPLETE (proof side wins) or ITEM_UNRESOLVED, separately from the coordinator answer.
- The record binds project id/tag, backup cursor + generation digest, and the selected anchorBindingDigest/incarnationRef/keyEpochRef; configuredClasses is written from the frozen table, never echoed from the caller.
- Copied data is frozen at every level (record, items, proofs, populations, upstream tuples). The caller's input object and its arrays are never frozen and never mutated. No secret, key, nonce or message field is read or stored.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the strict canonical codec and exact LF bridge. Encode a versioned, fixed-key-order, bounded UTF-8 JSON body with deterministic class/population/item ordering; compute SHA-256 over every body field except `recordDigest`, then append that digest. Decode with fatal UTF-8, exact keys/vocabularies/bounds/cardinalities, re-derived six-to-seven mapping and disposition invariants, digest recomputation, and byte-for-byte canonical re-encoding so whitespace, key order, duplicate keys, extensions, truncation, or any semantic byte mutation cannot become an alternate authoritative record. Return the stable unreadable upstream code/layer under coordinator UNKNOWN rather than throwing or defaulting.
implementationPlan.note:
Strict canonical codec landed at apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-inventory-codec.ts (310 physical lines, under the 400 split point) plus its exact LF bridge.

ENCODE: bodyObject() writes ONE fixed field order, built here and never spread from the caller's object, with deterministic class/population/item ordering inherited from the frozen mapping and the record builder's sort. recoveryReconciliationDigest computes SHA-256 (node:crypto, sync) over the body WITHOUT recordDigest; encodeRecoveryReconciliationRecord appends recordDigest last as UTF-8 JSON with no whitespace. That split is what makes the digest cover every bound leaf while remaining verifiable from the stored bytes alone.

DECODE is layered, and the ORDER of the layers is the design:
1. empty/over-bound bytes, fatal-UTF-8 decode failure, or JSON.parse failure -> RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_UNREADABLE.
2. structural validation -> RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_NONCANONICAL. orderedKeys() checks key ORDER, not merely the key set, at every level (record, proof, item, upstream tuple). configuredClasses must be the frozen six in order; proofs must be exactly six rows in class order whose populations equal the frozen row element-for-element (the six-to-seven mapping is RE-DERIVED, never trusted from the stored bytes); items are checked against the mapping, the disposition vocabulary, hex64/nullable-hex64/nullable-text field shapes, and two cross-checks (ADOPTED implies a restored intent ref, UNKNOWN implies an upstream tuple); every proof's itemCount is recomputed from the items; truth UNKNOWN, the coordinator pair and the record upstream must be present together or absent together, and the coordinator pair may only ever be {UNKNOWN_TRUTH, RECOVERY_INVENTORY}.
3. digest recomputation over the re-derived body -> RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH.
4. byte-for-byte canonical re-encode compare -> NONCANONICAL.
Layer 4 is what actually kills the duplicate-key and whitespace variants: JSON.parse silently keeps the last duplicate, so the parsed object looks legitimate and only re-encoding reveals the second spelling. Layer 3 catches the opposite case, a mutation that is still perfectly canonical. Neither layer alone is sufficient, which is why both exist.
Nothing throws and nothing defaults: every failure returns the frozen refusal carrying coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY plus its own upstream code at RECOVERY_INVENTORY.

TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED THIS STEP, both of the "assertion detached from its subject" family epic rail 6 names:
1. PRODUCTION BUG, caught by a red test: RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CLASS_EXTRA was UNREACHABLE. Only six class names exist, so any list longer than six is necessarily also a duplicate, and the duplicate guard answered first — the test asked for EXTRA and got DUPLICATE. Fixed by asking LENGTH first in refuseConfiguredClasses, with a comment recording why the order is load-bearing. All four mapping codes are now individually reachable and individually asserted.
2. TEST BUG, caught before it could pass vacuously: the mapping-strip case used .replace('"PROVIDER_RUN",', "") whose FIRST match is an item's `population` value, not the proofs row — that would have produced broken JSON and been answered by the UNREADABLE guard while reading as coverage of the mapping re-derivation. Retargeted to `,"PROVIDER_RUN"]`, which occurs only in the proofs populations array, with expect(text.split(...)).toHaveLength(2) asserting the anchor is unique before the mutation is applied. It now pins RECORD_NONCANONICAL exactly.

implementationPlan.description: Implement content-addressed durable persistence/readback and its exact LF bridge using only the existing public `SqliteEventStore` transaction surface—no schema change or raw SQLite. The write service must read the fixed ACTIVE recovery binding from the project store and the exact anchored incarnation, cross-check key epoch/project/backup generation, and only then build the record; it must accept no request-selected current refs. Commit canonical bytes once under a domain-separated record-digest aggregate with command kind `recovery.reconcile_external`, expectedVersion 0, exact domain schema/event IDs, and identical request/result/event bytes; exact retries replay one event. The reader addresses an explicit record digest (never an invented 'latest'), verifies the sole sequence-1 event plus decision trace/decision bytes and codec/digest/aggregate identity, and maps absent, conflicting, malformed, or unverifiable evidence to `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`/`RECOVERY_INVENTORY` while retaining `RECORD_NOT_FOUND|UNREADABLE|CONFLICT` at `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER`. R3 may later bind this immutable digest; this task grants no recovery.complete authority.
implementationPlan.note:
Content-addressed durable persistence/readback landed at apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-inventory-ledger.ts (282 lines) plus its exact LF bridge. NO store schema change and NO raw SQLite: it uses only the existing public commitExpectedVersionDecision / readAggregateEvents / getCommandDecision surface, exactly as recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts already does.

WRITE (recordRecoveryReconciliation):
- Reads the exact 6-key external facts and 4-key scope through exactDataRecord; a smuggled incarnationRef/keyEpochRef makes the key set inexact and refuses INPUT_INVALID at RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER. The caller CANNOT nominate current refs.
- Selected authority comes from the store: readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding (fixed ACTIVE slot) then readAnchoredIncarnation for that exact incarnation. Missing/unreadable binding -> RECOVERY_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE; unanchored incarnation -> RECOVERY_ANCHOR_UNAVAILABLE. Three cross-checks then run before any record exists: anchored keyEpochRef vs ACTIVE keyEpochRef, anchored incarnationRef vs ACTIVE incarnationRef, and anchored backupGenerationDigest vs the supplied one — each -> RECOVERY_BINDING_MISMATCH.
- Only then is the record built, with selected = the ANCHORED bindingDigest/incarnationRef/keyEpochRef. A record-layer refusal is returned unchanged, keeping its own RECOVERY_INVENTORY upstream rather than being restamped as a ledger fault.
- Commits canonical bytes ONCE: command kind recovery.reconcile_external, domain-separated aggregate recovery-reconciliation:<recordDigest>, expectedVersion 0, deterministic commandId recovery-reconcile:<recordDigest> and eventId <commandId>:recorded, domainSchemaVersion moe-recovery-reconciliation/1, and IDENTICAL request/result/event bytes. An exact retry replays: the second call returns disposition REPLAYED and readAggregateEvents still shows exactly one event at sequence 1.
- Deliberately NO try/catch around the commit, following the house precedent recorded in recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts: a genuine store fault must keep throwing, because reporting a real database failure as a benign refusal is how a recovery ledger gains false authority.
- Returns authority "NONE". There is no completion/approval field; R3 may later bind this immutable digest, and nothing here grants recovery.complete.

READ (readRecoveryReconciliation) addresses ONE explicit digest — there is no "latest" and no mutable pointer, because a repointable pointer would be exactly the unspecified authority this area must not create. It verifies, in order: at most two events fetched so a second event is DETECTED rather than truncated away; zero events -> RECORD_NOT_FOUND; more than one -> RECORD_CONFLICT; the sole event must be aggregateSequence 1 with the right eventType and a decisionTrace whose commandKind and projectId match; the decision addressed by that trace must exist, be EFFECTS_COMMITTED, sit on this aggregate, carry this command kind, and its resultBytes must equal the event payload byte for byte (a row whose result disagrees with the event it committed is evidence of nothing, and picking one of the two would be inventing a fact); the bytes must decode under the strict codec, else RECORD_UNREADABLE; and the decoded recordDigest must equal the ADDRESS and its projectId the queried project, else RECORD_CONFLICT — content addressing is only real if the address is checked. Store read faults are caught to RECORD_UNREADABLE. Every refusal answers coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH at RECOVERY_INVENTORY while retaining its ledger code at RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER.

FOUR TYPE ERRORS found by tsc and fixed, one of them a real fail-open:
- codec readRecord was validating the persisted coordinator pair with readUpstream, whose vocabulary is the 24 UPSTREAM codes. "UNKNOWN_TRUTH" is not among them, so the guard could never have accepted a legitimate coordinator — and the comparison tsc flagged as having no overlap was the symptom. Replaced with a dedicated readCoordinator that admits exactly the one pair {UNKNOWN_TRUTH, RECOVERY_INVENTORY}. Reusing the upstream reader would have admitted any of the 24 codes as a coordinator answer.
- contract isDataProperty treated `enumerable: boolean | undefined` as boolean; now `=== true`.
- Two test fixtures widened a literal upstream code to `string`; pinned with `as const`.

VERIFICATION (fresh, foreground): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 with no diagnostics. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/recovery/recovery-inventory-record.test.ts src/recovery/recovery-inventory-ledger.test.ts src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` => "Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 49 passed (49)". runtime-entrypoint.test.ts is included on purpose: it is the guard that would redden if any of the five new .js bridges were missing, misnamed or byte-wrong, so its green is the bridge evidence. Mutation drills are step 7 — nothing is claimed proven until each named test has been shown to go red.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of the owned diff as a trust boundary.

STATIC CHECKS (all measured, none asserted from memory):
- Per-file physical lines (`grep -c ''`, which does not undercount like PowerShell Measure-Object): contract 255, subject 296, record 244, codec 321, ledger 282. ALL under the 400 hard split point; three exceed the 250 target and I am disclosing that rather than manufacturing artificial seams. Test files are not production sources and are uncapped.
- All FIVE .js bridges verified with `cat -A`: each is exactly `export * from "./<name>.ts";$` — one LF-terminated line, byte-identical to expectedBridgeSource in runtime-entrypoint.test.ts. That test is in the focused run and is green, so the bridge set is proven, not assumed.
- Diff scope: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/recovery packages/store/src` lists exactly the twelve owned paths, ALL as `??` (new). Zero pre-existing files modified, zero store schema change, zero foreign paths.
- Secrets: grep for signatureHex|publicKeySpki|challengeDigest|keyHandle|secret|token|privateKey|nonce over all five production sources returns nothing. The only `payload` hits are the store event payload carrying our own canonical record bytes. The ledger touches the anchored binding at exactly six sites and reads only bindingDigest/incarnationRef/keyEpochRef/backupGenerationDigest — no key material, no signature, no SPKI, ever serialized.
- Caller objects: grep for Object.freeze applied to an argument returns nothing; exactDataRecord freezes a NEW object built by Object.fromEntries. The record suite asserts positively that the caller's input and its subjects array are NOT frozen.
- Combined proof stored once: the provider proof is one row declaring two populations; the digest-sensitivity and cardinality tests both pin it.
- No COMPLETE synthesis: drill (h) below proves it.
- Windows handles: the ledger suite's afterEach drains EVERY opened handle via a stack and closes before rmSync; the reopen test closes both the contender and the original before reopening.

MUTATION DRILLS — 11 run, 11 RED, each byte-restored and sha256-verified. Every drill asserted its anchor appeared EXACTLY ONCE before mutating (a missed anchor aborts rather than silently running the suite on pristine code and reading as green), and every restore was verified by comparing the sha256 of the file after restore to the sha256 taken before the mutation.
  a1 delete the PROVIDER_RUN mapping edge -> "covers the seven design populations..." RED
  a2 same edge -> "maps every population exactly once..." RED
  b  drop projectTag from the canonical digest body -> "changes the record digest for every bound body field" RED
  c  bypass the adoption incarnation equality -> "quarantines each single adoption deviation..." RED
  d1 bypass the adoption key-epoch equality -> same test RED
  d2 bypass the ledger anchored-vs-ACTIVE key-epoch check -> "refuses when the ACTIVE key epoch disagrees..." RED
  e  drop the reader's recordDigest-equals-address check -> "refuses a record filed under another digest's aggregate" RED
  f  widen the ledger fact key set to accept incarnationRef/keyEpochRef -> "accepts no caller-selected current refs" RED
  g  drop the codec's canonical re-encode byte compare -> "refuses non-canonical byte variants" RED
  h  raise a missing configured proof slot to COMPLETE -> "fills a missing configured proof with an UNKNOWN slot" RED
  i  drop the sole-event conflict guard -> "refuses a second event under one record aggregate" RED
One drill (d1) initially ABORTED on anchor count 0 — a wrong-indentation anchor, exactly the failure mode where a mutator that applied nothing runs the suite on pristine code and reads as a holding guard. The harness caught it by design; the anchor was corrected against the real bytes (`grep -n | cat -A`) and rerun to RED.

ADVERSARIAL CHECKLIST, items considered and their resolution:
- CONCURRENCY: two concurrent identical writes are serialized by the store on (commandId, principalId, projectId) with expectedVersion 0 on a digest-keyed aggregate; the second replays rather than forking. There is no check-then-act: nothing reads-then-writes and hopes. Two concurrent DIFFERENT records simply address different aggregates. The reopen/two-handle test exercises real contention.
- INPUTS: null/undefined/array/proxy/accessor inputs all refuse INPUT_INVALID via own-descriptor reading; oversized arrays refuse at MAX_RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_ITEMS and oversized bytes at MAX_RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_BYTES; empty bytes and invalid UTF-8 refuse RECORD_UNREADABLE; identity strings are NFC-normalised and control/format characters are rejected, so a homoglyph or zero-width variant cannot masquerade as a duplicate identity.
- TOCTOU: the reader re-verifies decision-vs-event bytes and re-checks the content address, so a row that changed between the event read and the decision read cannot be answered with.
- SIDE EFFECTS: the write is a single store transaction; there is no part

planningNotes.risks: The runner registration factories preserve only aggregate inventory code/layer, not the deeper Git/artifact observer refusal; retain exactly what production exposes and never invent deeper provenance. `readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding` collapses missing/unreadable to null, so the ledger must fail closed with a local upstream code rather than claim a selected binding. Missing configured evidence is a valid persisted UNKNOWN slot, whereas a malformed configured class set is a structural refusal—do not conflate the two. Content-addressed persistence intentionally supplies no current/latest selection and no recovery completion authority. Preserve foreign work and stage/commit only the ten named paths.
